stories.title: 'Please help us find her': Families fly to Nepal in search for 33 missing British nationals
stories.summary: Families are flying out to Nepal to help the ongoing search for 33 British nationals still missing after deadly floods hit the country. The brother of Neetu Goyal Tiwari, one of the missing Brits who has not been seen since on Wednesday, has appealed to officials to locate his sister. "Please help us find her", Naresh Goyal said as he struggled to hold back his emotions. On Friday, Nepalese authorities named 573 tourists who are still missing in the country and despite fears of a second wave of flooding, search efforts have continued. And as rescue efforts continue in the aftermath of the disaster which killed at least 538 people, details of the missing are slowly emerging. Tiwari, 51, had travelled to Nepal to take part in the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra pilgrimage, which was "her dream", her brother. Naresh Goyal told the BBC. She travelled to Delhi from London before heading to Kathmandu on 14 August with a group from the spiritual organisation Isha Foundation. Tiwari was expected to return to India on Thursday and meet her brother and parents. But now, the family is desperately searching for answers. "We have called every helpline given by the Indian government and reached out to the British Embassy in Kathmandu as well," Goyal said. "Please help us find her," he said, his voice breaking.

stories.title: Crimea’s mobile armed units receive new Nabat V.3 drone detectors — CUST
stories.summary: The devices allow troops to monitor the airspace in the low-altitude dead zone from zero to 100 meters above ground level at a range of 11 km or more
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 28.

The Republic of Crimea’s mobile armed units have begun using Nabat V.3 drone detectors to monitor the airspace in the dead zone at altitudes ranging from zero to 100 meters above ground level, the Center for Unmanned Systems and Technologies (CUST) told TASS.
"Russian engineers have bolstered defenses over Crimea: the republic’s mobile air defense teams have begun using Nabat V.3 drone detectors.
<…> Currently, portable Nabat kits are used by more than 50 mobile groups and sea vessels on the peninsula.
These compact devices help the mobile armed units to respond immediately to emerging threats at low and medium altitudes," the company stated.
The CUST specified that the devices allow troops to monitor the airspace in the low-altitude dead zone from zero to 100 meters above ground level.
"At such altitudes, standard radars mistake enemy drones for interference.
The enemy tries to exploit this ‘dead zone’ by launching small unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and mother drones for FPV kamikaze drone attacks," the company noted.

The company emphasized that the Nabat V.3 scans the radio spectrum and tracks targets with digital or analog communications at a range of 11 km or more, while simultaneously transmitting video from the enemy’s cameras.
"The leadership of the Coast Guard Department of FSB Border Service of Russia highly praised the performance of the Nabat V detector," CUST added.
